section.content: 提供一种能够预测制造时的三维造型物的变形的机器学习装置。机器学习装置具备：数据获取部，获取第一数据和第二数据，所述第一数据包含表示三维造型物的目标形状的形状数据和表示为了抑制制造中的三维造型物的变形而向三维造型物追加的追加部分的目标形状的追加形状数据，所述第二数据是与三维造型物的变形相关的数据；存储部，存储学习数据集，所述学习数据集包含多个第一数据和多个第二数据；以及学习部，通过执行使用了学习数据集的机器学习，学习第一数据与第二数据的关系。

Provided is a machine learning device capable of predicting deformation of a three-dimensional modeling object at the time of manufacturing. The machine learning device is provided with: a data acquisition unit that acquires first data including shape data representing a target shape of a three-dimensional modeling object and additional shape data representing a target shape of an additional portion to be added to the three-dimensional modeling object in order to suppress deformation of the three-dimensional modeling object during manufacturing, and second data relating to deformation of the three-dimensional modeling object; a storage unit that stores a learning data set including a plurality of first data and a plurality of second data; and a learning unit that learns the relationship between the first data and the second data by performing machine learning using the learning data set.

Machine learning deviceTechnical Field

The present disclosure relates to a machine learning device.

Background

There is known a technique of laminating materials including powdery metal and ceramic to mold a three-dimensional molded article, and then sintering the three-dimensional molded article to improve strength. Since the three-dimensional molded object shrinks due to sintering, deformation, cracking, warpage, and the like may occur in the three-dimensional molded object after sintering. Regarding this problem, patent document 1 describes the following technique: the deformation amount of the three-dimensional modeling object caused by heat is predicted by using a finite element method, and when the predicted deformation amount is not within an allowable range, the input geometry is corrected, and the three-dimensional modeling object is modeled according to the corrected input geometry, thereby suppressing the deformation of the three-dimensional modeling object.

Prior art literature

Patent literature

Patent document 1: japanese patent application laid-open No. 2017-53027.

Disclosure of Invention

Problems to be solved by the invention

In the technique for predicting the deformation amount of a three-dimensional modeling object using the finite element method as in patent document 1, when predicting the deformation amount due to heat of a three-dimensional modeling object having a complex shape such as being modeled by a three-dimensional modeling apparatus, it is necessary to set the mesh of an analysis model to be thin, and the analysis time is long. Such a problem is common not only in the case of manufacturing a three-dimensional shaped article by stacking powdery metals and the like and then sintering them, but also in the case of manufacturing a three-dimensional shaped article by stacking plasticized thermoplastic resins.

Means for solving the problems

According to one aspect of the present disclosure, a machine learning device is provided. The machine learning device is provided with: a data acquisition unit that acquires first data including shape data indicating a target shape of a three-dimensional modeling object and additional shape data indicating a target shape of an additional portion to be added to the three-dimensional modeling object in order to suppress deformation of the three-dimensional modeling object during manufacturing, and second data related to deformation of the three-dimensional modeling object; a storage unit that stores a learning data set including a plurality of the first data and a plurality of the second data; and a learning unit that learns a relationship between the first data and the second data by performing machine learning using the learning data set.

Symbol description

Detailed Description

A. First embodiment:

fig. 1 is an explanatory diagram showing an outline configuration of a machine learning system 50 according to the first embodiment. The machine learning system 50 includes: machine learning device 100, information processing device 200, three-dimensional modeling device 300, heat treatment device 400, inspection device 500, and display device 600.

The machine learning device 100 is configured by a computer including one or more processors, a main storage device, and an input/output interface for inputting/outputting signals to/from the outside. In the present embodiment, the machine learning device 100 generates a learning model by executing learning processing described later, and predicts a manufacturing error of a three-dimensional modeling object using the learning model by executing prediction processing described later. The machine learning device 100 may be configured by a plurality of computers.

In the present embodiment, the machine learning device 100 includes: the data acquisition unit 110, the data storage unit 120, the calculation unit 130, the preprocessing unit 140, the learning unit 150, the learning model storage unit 160, and the prediction unit 170.

The data acquisition section 110 acquires first data from the information processing apparatus 200, the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300, and the heat treatment apparatus 400 by wired communication or wireless communication. Further, the data acquisition unit 110 acquires the second data from the inspection device 500 by wired communication or wireless communication. Details regarding the first data and the second data will be described later.

The data storage unit 120 stores various data such as the first data and the second data. The arithmetic unit 130 generates manufacturing error data described later using the first data and the second data. The preprocessing section 140 generates a learning data set using the first data and the manufacturing error data. In the learning process, the learning unit 150 performs machine learning using the learning data set to generate a learning model. In the present embodiment, the learning unit 150 includes: a bonus calculation unit 151 and a cost function update unit 152. The learning model storage 160 stores a learning model. The prediction unit 170 predicts a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object using the learning model in the prediction process.

The information processing apparatus 200 is configured by a computer including one or more processors, a main storage device, and an input/output interface for inputting/outputting signals to/from the outside. In the present embodiment, the information processing apparatus 200 generates shape data and additional shape data by three-dimensional CAD software installed in advance. The shape data represents a target shape of the main body portion of the three-dimensional modeling object. The additional shape data indicates a target shape of an additional portion to be added to the main body portion in order to suppress deformation of the main body portion during the production of the three-dimensional shaped object. The target shape refers to a shape that is a target at the time of manufacturing of the product. That is, in the case of manufacturing a product in accordance with the target shape, the manufacturing error of the product is zero. When the targeted shapes and sizes of the main body portion of the product a and the main body portion of the product B are different, the targeted shapes of the main body portions of the two are different. When the shapes, sizes, numbers, and arrangements of the additional portions of the product a and the additional portions of the product B as targets are different from each other, the target shapes of the additional portions are different from each other. The shape data and the additional shape data are transmitted to the machine learning device 100. Further, in the present embodiment, the information processing apparatus 200 reads shape data and additional shape data by using pre-installed slicing software to generate modeling data. The molding data represents various pieces of information for controlling the three-dimensional molding device 300 to mold a three-dimensional molded object of a desired shape. The modeling data is sent to the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300.

The three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 models the three-dimensional modeling object based on the modeling data. In the present embodiment, the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 is a three-dimensional modeling apparatus of an adhesive injection system. The structure of the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 will be described later.

The heat treatment apparatus 400 performs heat treatment on the three-dimensional shaped object shaped by the three-dimensional shaping apparatus 300. In the present embodiment, the heat treatment apparatus 400 is a sintering furnace. The heat treatment apparatus 400 sinters the three-dimensional shaped object according to preset heat treatment conditions. The heat treatment conditions include, for example, heating time, heating temperature, and the like.

The inspection apparatus 500 measures the size of the three-dimensional modeling object after the heat treatment, and generates measurement data. In the present embodiment, the inspection apparatus 500 is a three-dimensional measuring machine. In the present embodiment, the measurement data indicates the shape of the three-dimensional shaped object after the heat treatment. The measurement data may also indicate the strain amount, warpage amount, presence or absence of cracks, and the like of the three-dimensional shaped object after heat treatment.

The display device 600 displays the prediction result of the prediction unit 170 of the machine learning device 100. In this embodiment mode, the display device is a liquid crystal display. The display device 600 is not limited to a liquid crystal display, and may be a plasma display, an organic EL display, or the like, for example.

Fig. 2 is an explanatory diagram showing a schematic configuration of the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300. The three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 includes a control unit 301, a table unit 302, a moving mechanism 303, and a modeling unit 304. The control unit 301 is configured by a computer having one or more processors, a main storage device, and an input/output interface for inputting/outputting signals to/from the outside. The control unit 301 controls the table unit 302, the moving mechanism 303, and the modeling unit 304 based on modeling data supplied from the information processing apparatus 200.

The table unit 302 includes: a table 310, a frame 315 surrounding the outer periphery of the table 310, and a lifting mechanism 316 for moving the table 310 in the Z-axis direction. In the present embodiment, the lifting mechanism 316 is constituted by an actuator that moves the table 310 in the Z-axis direction under the control of the control unit 301.

The moving mechanism 303 is provided above the table unit 302. The moving mechanism 303 supports the modeling unit 304 and relatively moves the modeling unit 304 with respect to the table 310 in the X-axis direction. In the present embodiment, the moving mechanism 303 is constituted by an actuator that moves the modeling unit 304 in the X-axis direction under the control of the control unit 301.

The modeling unit 304 is disposed above the stage unit 302. The molding unit 304 includes a material supply unit 320, a flattening unit 330, a liquid supply unit 340, and a curing energy supply unit 350. In the modeling unit 304, a material supply portion 320, a flattening portion 330, a liquid supply portion 340, and a curing energy supply portion 350 are arranged in this order from the-X axis direction side.

The material supply unit 320 supplies the powder material PD, which is a powdery material, to the table 310. In the present embodiment, the material supply unit 320 is constituted by a hopper for storing the powder material PD. The powder material PD is a raw material of the three-dimensional modeling object. As the powder material PD, powder of metal materials such as stainless steel, steel other than stainless steel, pure iron, titanium alloy, magnesium alloy, cobalt alloy, nickel alloy, and powder of ceramic materials such as silica, titania, alumina, zirconia, and silicon nitride can be used. One of them may be used as the powder material PD, or two or more of them may be used in combination. In the present embodiment, stainless steel powder is used as the powder material PD.

The flattening unit 330 flattens the powder material PD supplied from the material supply unit 320 onto the table 310. In the present embodiment, the flattening unit 330 is constituted by a roller. The excess amount of the powder material PD extruded from the table 310 by the flattening unit 330 is stored in the material recovery unit 317 provided in the frame 315. The flattening unit 330 may be constituted by a squeegee.

The liquid supply unit 340 includes a liquid supply source 341 as a supply source of the bonding liquid BD, and a liquid ejecting head 342 for ejecting the bonding liquid BD to the powder material PD flattened by the flattening unit 330. In the present embodiment, the liquid supply source 341 is constituted by a tank for storing the binding liquid BD. The bonding liquid BD is a liquid containing a bonding agent that bonds the powder materials PD to each other. As the binder, various photocurable resins such as thermoplastic resins, thermosetting resins, visible light curable resins that are cured by light in the visible light region, ultraviolet curable resins, infrared curable resins, and X-ray curable resins can be used. One of them may be used as a binder, or two or more of them may be used in combination. As the solvent of the binder, water or an organic solvent can be used. In this embodiment, a binding liquid BD containing an ultraviolet curable resin is used as a binder.

The liquid ejecting head 342 is configured by a piezoelectric driving type liquid ejecting head having a pressure chamber, a piezoelectric element that changes the volume of the pressure chamber, and a plurality of nozzle holes that communicate with the pressure chamber. The liquid ejecting head 342 deflects the side wall of the pressure chamber filled with the bonding liquid supplied from the liquid supply source 341 by the piezoelectric element, reduces the volume of the pressure chamber, and ejects the bonding liquid BD from the nozzle hole in an amount corresponding to the reduction in the volume of the pressure chamber.

The curing energy supply unit 350 applies energy for curing the bonding agent contained in the bonding liquid BD ejected from the liquid supply unit 340 to the powder material PD. In the present embodiment, the curing energy supply unit 350 is constituted by an ultraviolet lamp. In the case of using a thermosetting binder, the curing energy supply unit 350 may be constituted by a heater.

Fig. 3 is an explanatory diagram showing an example of the target shape of the three-dimensional object OB. Fig. 4 is a cross-sectional view taken along line IV-IV of the three-dimensional object OB of fig. 3. The three-dimensional object OB shown in fig. 3 and 4 has a main body portion MP and two additional portions AP1 to AP2. In the following description, the additional portion AP1 is referred to as a first additional portion AP1, and the additional portion AP2 is referred to as a second additional portion AP2. In the description without distinguishing the first additional portion AP1 and the second additional portion AP2, the first additional portion AP1 and the second additional portion AP2 may be simply referred to as additional portion AP. In this example, the main body portion MP has a zigzag shape when viewed from the upper surface. A first through hole HL1 is provided at one end of the main body MP, a second through hole HL2 is provided at the other end of the main body MP, and a third through hole HL3 is provided at the center of the main body MP. The first additional portion AP1 and the second additional portion AP2 have a cylindrical shape centered on a central axis along the Z-axis direction. The first additional portion AP1 and the second additional portion AP2 are connected to the bottom surface of the main body portion MP. The first additional portion AP1 is disposed beside the first through hole HL1, and the second additional portion AP2 is disposed beside the second through hole HL 2. The first additional portion AP1 and the second additional portion AP2 are disposed so as to sandwich the third through hole HL3.

Fig. 5 is a flowchart showing a method for manufacturing the three-dimensional object OB in the present embodiment. The method of manufacturing the three-dimensional object OB is described with reference to the case of manufacturing the three-dimensional object OB shown in fig. 3 and 4. First, in the molding data acquisition step of step S110 in fig. 5, the control unit 301 of the three-dimensional molding apparatus 300 acquires molding data from the information processing apparatus 200.

In the molding step of step S120, as shown in fig. 2, the control unit 301 controls the molding unit 304, the moving mechanism 303, and the lifting mechanism 316 of the table unit 302 based on the molding data, thereby molding the three-dimensional molded object OB on the table 310. In the initial state, the modeling unit 304 is disposed on the +x axis direction side of the stage 310. The control unit 301 controls the movement mechanism 303 to move the modeling unit 304 in the-X axis direction. The control unit 301 supplies the powder material PD from the material supply unit 320 to the stage 310 while moving the modeling unit 304 in the-X axis direction, planarizes the powder material PD supplied to the stage 310 by the planarizer 330, ejects the bonding liquid BD from the liquid supply unit 340 to a position corresponding to the target shape of the three-dimensional modeling object OB on the powder material PD, and cures the bonding agent contained in the bonding liquid BD by the curing energy supply unit 350. And curing by the bonding agent to form an nth layer of the three-dimensional modeling object OB. n is an arbitrary natural number. Thereafter, the control unit 301 controls the movement mechanism 303 to return the modeling unit 304 to the position on the +x axis direction side of the table 310, and controls the lifting mechanism 316 to lower the table 310 by the thickness of the nth layer. By repeating the above-described processing, the control unit 301 stacks the n+1th layer on the n-th layer, and molds the three-dimensional molded object OB having the main body portion MP and the additional portions AP1 to AP 2.

Fig. 6 is a plan view showing an example of the three-dimensional object OB placed on the carrier ST. In the supporting step of step S130 in fig. 5, the three-dimensional modeling object OB is taken out from the three-dimensional modeling apparatus 300 and placed on the carrier ST as shown in fig. 6. The carrier ST is a plate-like member formed of a ceramic material or the like. In this example, two slits SL1 to SL2 are provided in the carrier ST. In the following description, the slit SL1 is referred to as a first slit SL1, and the slit SL2 is referred to as a second slit SL2. In the case where the description is made without distinguishing the first slit SL1 and the second slit SL2 in particular, the first slit SL1 and the second slit SL2 may be simply referred to as the slit SL. The first slit SL1 and the second slit SL2 have a longitudinal direction along the X-axis direction. The three-dimensional object OB is placed on the placement device ST such that the first additional portion AP1 provided on the three-dimensional object OB is inserted into the first slit SL1 and the second additional portion AP2 is inserted into the second slit SL2.

In the heat treatment step of step S140 in fig. 5, heat treatment is performed on the three-dimensional modeling object OB. In the present embodiment, the three-dimensional shaped object OB placed on the carrier ST is heated under predetermined heat treatment conditions by the heat treatment apparatus 400, whereby the binder is degreased from the three-dimensional shaped object OB, and the three-dimensional shaped object OB is sintered. By sintering, the three-dimensional object OB is shrunk, and the strength of the three-dimensional object OB is improved.

In the inspection step of step S150, the inspection device 500 measures the dimension of the three-dimensional modeling object OB after the heat treatment step, and generates measurement data. The measurement data is transmitted to the machine learning device 100. After the step S150, the method of manufacturing the three-dimensional shaped object OB ends. The additional portions AP1 to AP2 are removed from the three-dimensional object OB between the heat treatment step in step S140 and the inspection step in step S150 or after the heat treatment step in step S150.

Fig. 7 is a plan view showing an example of the three-dimensional shaped object OB after the heat treatment process. Fig. 7 shows a three-dimensional shaped object OB after the heat treatment process using the carrier ST shown in fig. 6. In this example, since the movement of the first additional portion AP1 in the Y-axis direction is restricted by the first slit SL1 and the movement of the second additional portion AP2 in the Y-axis direction is restricted by the second slit SL2, the moment about the central axis in the Z-axis direction due to the shrinkage of the three-dimensional object OB in the heat treatment step is suppressed from acting on the outer peripheral portion of the third through hole HL3 in the main body portion MP. Therefore, deformation of the outer peripheral portion of the third through hole HL3 is suppressed.

When the shape, size, arrangement of the additional portions AP1 to AP2 of the three-dimensional object OB or the shape, size, arrangement of the slits SL1 to SL2 of the carrier ST are inappropriate, for example, a moment about the central axis along the Z-axis direction acts, and as shown by the two-dot chain line in fig. 7, the shape of the outer peripheral portion of the third through hole HL3 is deformed, and the manufacturing error of the main body portion MP of the three-dimensional object OB may exceed the allowable range.

Fig. 8 is a first explanatory diagram showing test results for investigating the dimensional accuracy of the three-dimensional modeling object OB. Fig. 9 is a plan view showing sample 2 placed on carrier ST. Fig. 8 shows the results of examining the dimensional accuracy of the main body MP for samples 1 to 4 of 4 three-dimensional objects OB produced by varying the orientation of the slits SL1 to SL2 of the carrier ST in the longitudinal direction. For each of samples 1 to 4, when the manufacturing error of the main body portion MP is within the allowable range, in other words, when the dimensional accuracy of the main body portion MP is good, the symbol "a" is used, and when the manufacturing error of the main body portion MP exceeds the allowable range, in other words, when the dimensional accuracy of the main body portion MP is poor, the symbol "B" is used.

The shape, material, and heat treatment conditions were the same for each of samples 1 to 4. In the production of the sample 1, as shown in fig. 6, a heat treatment process is performed using a carrier ST having a first slit SL1 and a second slit SL2 and having a longitudinal direction along the X-axis direction. In the production of the sample 2, as shown in fig. 9, the heat treatment process is performed using a carrier ST in which the first slit SL1 has a longitudinal direction along the X-axis direction and the second slit SL2 has a longitudinal direction along the Y-axis direction. In the production of the sample 3, the heat treatment process was performed using a carrier ST having the first slit SL1 and the second slit SL2 and having a longitudinal direction along the Y-axis direction. In the production of the sample 4, the heat treatment process was performed using a carrier ST in which the first slit SL1 has a length direction along the Y-axis direction and the second slit SL2 has a length direction along the X-axis direction. The manufacturing error of the main body portion MP of the sample 1 is within the allowable range. On the other hand, the manufacturing error of the main body portion MP of samples 2 to 4 exceeds the allowable range.

Fig. 10 is a second explanatory diagram showing test results for investigating the dimensional accuracy of the three-dimensional modeling object OB. Fig. 11 is a plan view showing sample 8 placed on carrier ST. Fig. 10 shows the results of examining the dimensional accuracy of the main body portion MP for samples 5 to 8 of 4 three-dimensional shaped objects OB produced by different arrangements of the additional portions AP1 to AP 2. In fig. 10, the meaning of the symbol "a" or "B" used to indicate whether or not the dimensional accuracy is good is the same as the meaning of the symbol "a" or "B" used to indicate whether or not the dimensional accuracy is good in fig. 8.

The materials and heat treatment conditions were the same for each of samples 5 to 8. In the production of each of the samples 5 to 8, the heat treatment process was performed using a carrier ST having a longitudinal direction along the X-axis direction in which the first slit SL1 and the second slit SL2 were provided. In each of the samples 5 to 8, the center point Pa1 of the first additional portion AP1, the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3, and the center point Pa2 of the second additional portion AP2 are arranged in this order along the X-axis direction. In each of the samples 5 to 8, the position of the center point Pa1 of the first additional portion AP1 in the Y-axis direction, the position of the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 in the Y-axis direction, and the position of the center point Pa2 of the second additional portion AP2 in the Y-axis direction are the same. In each of the samples 5 to 8, the distance Lh1 in the X-axis direction between the center point Ph1 of the first through-hole HL1 and the center point Ph3 of the third through-hole HL3 was 40.0mm, and the distance Lh2 in the X-axis direction between the center point Ph2 of the second through-hole HL2 and the center point Ph3 of the third through-hole HL3 was 40.0mm.

In sample 5, the distance La1 in the X-axis direction between the center point Pa1 of the first additional portion AP1 and the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 was 27.5mm, and the distance La2 in the X-axis direction between the center point Pa2 of the second additional portion AP2 and the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 was 27.5mm. In sample 6, the distance La1 in the X-axis direction between the center point Pa1 of the first additional portion AP1 and the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 was 40.0mm, and the distance La2 in the X-axis direction between the center point Pa2 of the second additional portion AP2 and the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 was 40.0mm. That is, in sample 6, as shown in fig. 6, the first additional portion AP1 and the second additional portion AP2 are arranged. In sample 7, the distance La1 in the X-axis direction between the center point Pa1 of the first additional portion AP1 and the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 was 52.5mm, and the distance La2 in the X-axis direction between the center point Pa2 of the second additional portion AP2 and the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 was 52.5mm. In sample 8, the distance La1 in the X-axis direction between the center point Pa1 of the first additional portion AP1 and the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 was 40.0mm, and the distance La2 in the X-axis direction between the center point Pa2 of the second additional portion AP2 and the center point Ph3 of the third through hole HL3 was 52.5mm. That is, in sample 8, as shown in fig. 11, the first additional portion AP1 and the second additional portion AP2 are arranged. The manufacturing errors of the main body portions MP of samples 5 to 6 are within the allowable range. On the other hand, the manufacturing errors of the main body portions MP of samples 7 to 8 exceeded the allowable range.

Fig. 12 is a flowchart showing the content of the learning process. This process is performed by the machine learning device 100 at the timing when the production of one three-dimensional modeling object OB ends, for example. First, in step S210, the data acquisition section 110 acquires first data. The first data includes shape data indicating a target shape of the main body portion MP of the three-dimensional object OB and additional shape data indicating a target shape of the additional portion AP. In the present embodiment, the first data further includes material data indicating information about a material used in the molding process and heat treatment condition data indicating heat treatment conditions in the heat treatment process. The material data indicates, for example, the type, physical properties, particle size, and the like of the powder material PD. When two or more materials are used as the powder material PD in combination, the type, physical properties, particle size, and content of each material in the powder material PD may be expressed. The material data may also indicate the type, physical properties, content of the binding agent, and the like of the binding liquid. The heat treatment condition data includes, for example, the position and longitudinal direction orientation of the slit SL of the carrier ST used in the heat treatment step, the heating time, the heating temperature, the heating speed, the number of times of heating, and the like in the heat treatment step. The acquired first data is stored in the data storage section 120.

In step S220, the data acquisition section 110 acquires second data. The second data includes measurement data generated in the inspection step. In the present embodiment, the measurement data indicates the shape of the three-dimensional modeling object OB after the heat treatment process. The acquired second data is stored in the data storage section 120 in association with the corresponding first data. The order of the processing of step S210 and the processing of step S220 may be reversed.

In step S230, the computing unit 130 reads the first data and the second data stored in the data storage unit 120, and generates manufacturing error data indicating an error between the size of the shape of the three-dimensional shaped object OB and the size of the target shape after the heat treatment step. The generated manufacturing error data is stored in the data storage unit 120. In step S240, the preprocessing unit 140 reads the first data stored in the data storage unit 120 and the manufacturing error data associated with the first data, and generates a learning data set.

In step S250, the learning unit 150 reads the learning data set generated by the preprocessing unit 140, performs machine learning, and generates a learning model. In step S260, the learning model storage unit 160 stores the learning model generated by the learning unit 150. After that, the machine learning device 100 ends the process. The machine learning device 100 repeats this process at the end of the production of one three-dimensional modeling object OB at a time, thereby performing machine learning using a learning data set including data concerning a plurality of different three-dimensional modeling objects OB such as the target shape of the main body portion MP, the target shape of the additional portion AP, or the powder material PD, the heat treatment conditions, and the like, and updating the learning model. For example, the machine learning device 100 performs machine learning using a learning data set containing the following data, updates a learning model: as in the above-described samples 1 to 4, the data relating to the plurality of three-dimensional shaped objects OB having different heat treatment conditions, which are the longitudinal direction of the slit SL of the carrier ST, and as in the above-described samples 5 to 8, the data relating to the plurality of three-dimensional shaped objects OB having different target shapes of the portion AP are added.

The algorithm of the machine learning performed by the learning unit 150 in the above step S250 is not particularly limited, and for example, a known algorithm such as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, or reinforcement learning can be used. In the present embodiment, the learning unit 150 performs reinforcement learning described later. Reinforcement learning is a method of observing the current state of an environment in which a learning object exists, performing a predetermined action in the current state, repeating a cycle of giving some rewards to the action in a trial-and-error manner, and learning a countermeasure for maximizing the total amount of rewards as an optimal solution.

An example of the algorithm of reinforcement learning performed by the learning unit 150 is described. The algorithm of this example is known as Q learning (Q learning), and is a method of learning a function Q (s, a) indicating an operation value when an operation a is selected in a state s, using the state s of the operation subject and the operation a selectable by the operation subject in the state s as independent variables. The action a with the highest cost function Q in state s is selected as the optimal solution. The Q learning is started in a state where the correlation between the state s and the action a is unknown, and trial and error is repeatedly performed to select various actions a in an arbitrary state s, whereby the cost function Q is repeatedly updated to approach the optimal solution. Here, as a result of selecting the action a in the state s, when the environment, that is, the state s, is changed, weighting of the action a is obtained as the reward r corresponding to the change, and learning is guided so that the action a with the higher reward r is selected, whereby the cost function Q can be made to approach the optimal solution in a relatively short time.

When the learning unit 150 performs Q learning, the first data, which is the state variable S, and the manufacturing error data, which is the determination data D, correspond to the updated state S, how the operation of determining the target shape of the additional portion AP to be added to the target shape of the main portion MP in the current state corresponds to the updated operation a, and the prize R obtained by the prize calculating unit 151 corresponds to the updated prize R. Therefore, the cost function updating unit 152 repeatedly updates the function Q indicating the cost of the target shape of the additional portion AP added to the target shape of the main portion MP in the current state by Q learning using the prize R.

For example, when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB manufactured based on the determined target shape is smaller than the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB before modification after the target shape of the additional portion AP is determined, when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB manufactured based on the determined target shape is within the allowable range, or the like, the prize R obtained by the prize calculating unit 151 may be set to a positive prize R, and when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB manufactured based on the determined target shape is larger than the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB before modification after the target shape of the additional portion AP is determined, or when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB manufactured based on the determined target shape exceeds the allowable range, or the like, the prize R obtained by the prize calculating unit 151 may be set to a negative prize R.

When Q learning is advanced using the reward R corresponding to the manufacturing error of the manufactured three-dimensional modeling object OB, the learning is guided in the direction in which the action to obtain the higher reward R is selected, and the value of the action value, that is, the function Q, relating to the action performed in the current state is updated based on the state of the environment, that is, the state variable S, and the determination data D, which are changed as a result of executing the selected action in the current state. By repeating this update, the function Q is rewritten to have a larger value as the function Q is properly operated. In this way, the correlation between the current state of the unknown environment and the actions thereto is gradually known.

When a predetermined start command is supplied to the machine learning device 100, the machine learning device 100 executes the process. First, in step S310, the data acquisition section 110 acquires first data. The acquired first data is stored in the data storage section 120. In step S320, the prediction unit 170 reads the first data stored in the data storage unit 120 and the learning model stored in the learning model storage unit 160, predicts a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB manufactured based on the first data, and generates prediction result data indicating a prediction result. According to the machine learning device 100 of the present embodiment described above, in the learning process, the learning unit 150 generates a learning model capable of predicting the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB, and in the prediction process, the prediction unit 170 predicts whether the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB is within the allowable range using the learning model, and outputs the prediction result to the display device 600. Therefore, when the prediction result that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB exceeds the allowable range is output, the user can correct the target shape of the additional portion AP so that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional object OB falls within the allowable range, and thus the three-dimensional object OB can be manufactured with good dimensional accuracy.

In step S430, the correction unit 180 determines whether or not the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range. The correction unit 180 can determine whether or not the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range, using the prediction result data generated by the prediction unit 170 in step S420.

If it is not determined in step S430 that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range, the correction unit 180 corrects the target shape of the additional portion AP indicated by the additional shape data included in the first data in step S435. Thereafter, the process returns to step S420, and the prediction unit 170 reads the first data corrected for the additional shape data and the learning model, predicts a manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB manufactured based on the first data corrected for the additional shape data, and generates prediction result data indicating a prediction result. The prediction unit 170 and the correction unit 180 repeat the processing of step S435, step S420, and step S430 until it is determined in step S430 that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range.

When it is determined in step S430 that the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB manufactured based on the first data is within the allowable range, in step S440, the shape data, the additional shape data, and the prediction result data are output, and the process ends. According to the machine learning device 100b of the present embodiment described above, when the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object OB predicted by the prediction unit 170 exceeds the allowable range, the correction unit 180 corrects the target shape of the additional portion AP indicated by the additional shape data, and outputs the shape data, the corrected additional shape data, and the prediction result data. Therefore, by manufacturing the three-dimensional object OB using the shape data and the corrected additional shape data, it is possible to suppress manufacturing errors of the three-dimensional object OB from exceeding the allowable range. In the case of predicting the deformation amount of the three-dimensional modeling object having the through-hole and the concave portion by the finite element method, the boundary conditions set in the analysis model are complicated, and therefore, it is difficult to accurately predict the deformation amount. In the machine learning device 100b of the present embodiment and the machine learning device 100 of the first embodiment, since the deformation amount of the three-dimensional modeling object due to heat is predicted by machine learning without using the finite element method, it is possible to effectively suppress the manufacturing error of the three-dimensional modeling object having the through hole and the concave portion from exceeding the allowable range.
